dct_description_sm: In Polar Regions, bottom ice algal communities, which are mostly composed of pennate diatoms, are submitted to a wide range of irradiance from the onset of spring until the melt period. Algae have developed a suite of photoprotective mechanisms to prevent photoinhibition and oxidative stress caused by excess or fluctuating light conditions. Petrou et al. (2011) showed the plasticity and the different photoacclimation of Antarctic diatoms depending of their niche habitats. Thus ice algae in bottom ice and sinking algae could possess different capacities of photoprotection. Changes in light conditions will be intensified in the future due to the decrease in snow and ice thicknesses, so it is essential to better understand the mechanisms employed by ice algae to photoacclimate to higher irradiances.This project aims to compare interannually (2015-2016) the evolution of photoprotective properties between bottom ice algae, sinking algae and phytoplankton.
dct_title_s: Photosynthetic and photoprotective properties of ice algae, phytoplankton and sinking algae, 2016 (2nd year)
